No. Under the common law, a murderer forfeits only the benefit he would take by survivorship or inheritance from his victim, not his own separately owned interest; because the man and his purported second wife were never validly married (he was still married to his first wife), they could not hold the home as tenants by the entirety, so he retains his own ownership share subject to the estate's claims. The appellate court will therefore reverse insofar as the trial court stripped him of all ownership rights.

CONFIDENCE: 78
